facts.statement: The genus Rinchenia was established by Barsbold in 1997.
The species Rinchenia mongoliensis was originally classified as Oviraptor mongoliensis.
Rinchenia lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Mongolia.
facts.quote: lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous epoch in what is now Mongolia, Nemegt Formation

facts.statement: A nearly complete skeleton of Rinchenia was discovered in 1984 at the Altan Uul II locality in the Gobi Desert.
facts.quote: During 1984, a nearly complete oviraptorid skeleton was discovered at the Altan Uul II (or Altan Ula II) locality of the highly fossiliferous Nemegt Formation, Gobi Desert

facts.statement: Rinchen Barsbold initially described the specimen as the species Oviraptor mongoliensis in 1986.
facts.quote: Later on, Mongolian paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold in 1986 used the specimen to erect and describe a new species of Oviraptor: Oviraptor mongoliensis

facts.statement: Barsbold assigned the specimen to the new genus Rinchenia in 1997.
facts.quote: Barsbold in 1997 assigned a new genus for the specimen, namely Rinchenia

facts.statement: The genus name Rinchenia honors Byambyn Rinchen, the father of the paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold.
facts.quote: The generic name, Rinchenia, is in honor of Byambyn Rinchen, veteran linguist and father of Barsbold

facts.statement: The species name mongoliensis refers to Mongolia, where the holotype was found.
facts.quote: The specific name, mongoliensis, refers to the country where the holotype was found: Mongolia

facts.statement: Rinchenia was a small dinosaur estimated to be 1.7 meters long and weigh about 25 kilograms.
facts.quote: Rinchenia was a small-sized oviraptorid, estimated at 1.7 m and a body mass of about 25 kg

facts.statement: Rinchenia possessed a well-preserved, cassowary-like casque on its skull that incorporated many bones not included in the crest of Oviraptor.
facts.quote: Rinchenia had a well-preserved, highly developed, cassowary-like casque/dome which incorporated many bones in the skull that are free of the crest in Oviraptor

facts.statement: Rinchenia is known from a single specimen consisting of a complete skull with lower jaw, partial vertebral column, forelimbs with partial shoulder girdle, hindlimbs, partial pelvis, and a furcula.
facts.quote: Rinchenia se conoce por un solo espécimen, GI 100/32A que consiste en un cráneo completo con la mandíbula inferior, una columna vertebral parcial, brazos y una faja de hombro parcial, miembros traseros y una pelvis parcial, y una a fúrcula

facts.statement: Rinchenia lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 million years ago in the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 70 millones de años, en el Campaniense

facts.statement: Rinchenia lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Rinchenia is classified within the family Oviraptoridae.
The genus authority for Rinchenia is attributed to Osmólska and colleagues in 2004.
A reexamination found differences significant enough to warrant separating Rinchenia from Oviraptor into its own genus.
facts.quote: a subsequent reexamination found differences significant enough to warrant a separate genus

facts.statement: Rinchenia's skeleton was constructed more lightly and less robustly than that of Oviraptor.
facts.quote: Su esqueleto estaba construido más ligeramente y menos robusto que el de Oviraptor
